plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (24-layer aperiodic HfO2/SiO2 stack) based on feedback directives. Four complementary routes explore: (1) constrained local refinement with ±15 nm step size from previous best candidate, (2) UV-centered quarter-wave initialization to strengthen 200-400 nm reflection, (3) increased layer count (28 layers) to test additional degrees of freedom, and (4) asymmetric topology with UV-reflective section near substrate. All routes maintain the 30-layer maximum, HfO2/SiO2 material restriction, and dual-band objectives. Parent_route_id is set to 'route_02' for all routes per refinement_chain instruction.

routes.title: Constrained Local Refinement with Bounded Step Size
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness updates to ±15 nm from the previous best candidate (opt_aperiodic_hfosio2_24l__gradien__ae5ad96294fa) will resolve coarse optimization jumps while preserving the dual-band spectral balance achieved in round 1.
routes.design_principle: Local refinement with bounded step size prevents large thickness deviations that disrupt established interference conditions. A gentle harmonic penalty toward quarter-wave optical thickness at 1150 nm guides the SWIR transmission band without constraining UV reflection design freedom.
routes.proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate. Total finite layers: 24 (12 HfO2 + 12 SiO2 pairs).
design_variables: Layer thicknesses with bounds set to previous_best_thickness ± 15 nm per layer
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2
theory_basis: Local optimization with bounded step size prevents disruption of established spectral features
expected_advantages: Reduces risk of large thickness jumps disrupting interference conditions
Quarter-wave bias at 1150 nm improves SWIR transmission phase alignment
known_risks: Bounded search may miss global optimum if previous candidate is in local minimum
Quarter-wave penalty may constrain UV reflection optimization
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Initialize thicknesses from previous best candidate: [94.47, 46.86, 107.74, 119.33, 69.47, 135.67, 62.26, 146.48, 103.59, 80.70, 116.30, 64.87, 124.88, 71.01, 107.35, 102.79, 139.41, 56.90, 101.47, 102.82, 125.76, 53.97, 84.85, 79.64] nm. Constrain each layer thickness to previous_value ± 15 nm bounds. Apply harmonic penalty toward quarter-wave optical thickness at 1150 nm center wavelength. Optimize for maximum mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm and maximum mean reflectance in 200-400 nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with local refinement settings. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 200-400 nm, 800-1500 nm. soft objectives: High transmission in 800-1500 nm band; High reflection in 200-400 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low transmission in 200-400 nm band; Low reflection in 800-1500 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layers <= 30; Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Feedback directive specifies constrained local refinement with ±15 nm step size from current best configuration to resolve coarse jumps observed in round 1.

routes.title: UV-Centered Quarter-Wave Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing from a quarter-wave stack centered at 300 nm (UV band center) will strengthen 200-400 nm reflection while maintaining 800-1500 nm transmission through subsequent aperiodic optimization.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks at UV center wavelength provide strong initial reflection in 200-400 nm band. Subsequent free optimization allows SWIR transmission band to develop without UV-centered constraints.
routes.proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate. Total finite layers: 24 (12 HfO2 + 12 SiO2 pairs).
design_variables: Layer thicknesses initialized at quarter-wave optical thickness for 300 nm, then fully optimized
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high reflectance at design wavelength
HfO2/SiO2 index contrast sufficient for UV reflection with 12 pairs
expected_advantages: Strong initial UV reflection from quarter-wave initialization
Full optimization freedom allows SWIR transmission to develop
Complementary to route_02_refine_local which starts from previous best
known_risks: UV-centered initialization may bias optimization away from SWIR transmission optimum
24 layers may be insufficient for both bands if quarter-wave constraint is too strong

routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 24 to 28 layers provides additional degrees of freedom to improve dual-band performance while remaining under the 30-layer manufacturing constraint.
routes.design_principle: Additional layer pairs increase design space for balancing UV reflection and SWIR transmission. Quarter-wave initialization at 1150 nm provides SWIR transmission baseline with freedom to optimize UV band.

routes.title: Asymmetric Stack with UV Section Near Substrate
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Placing UV-reflective layers near the substrate interface and SWIR-transmissive layers near the air interface creates asymmetric spectral response that may improve dual-band separation.
routes.design_principle: Asymmetric topology allows different optical functions in different stack regions. UV-reflective section near substrate uses thinner quarter-wave layers at 300 nm. SWIR-transmissive section near air uses thicker layers optimized for 1150 nm transmission.
routes.proposed_topology: 24-layer asymmetric stack: Air | [SWIR section: 12 layers HfO2/SiO2 alternating] | [UV section: 12 layers HfO2/SiO2 alternating] | Fused Silica substrate. Total finite layers: 24 (12 HfO2 + 12 SiO2 pairs, split into two functional sections).
design_variables: Layer thicknesses with UV section initialized at quarter-wave for 300 nm, SWIR section initialized at quarter-wave for 1150 nm, then fully optimized
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2
Asymmetric design may require different deposition rates per section
theory_basis: Asymmetric multilayer designs can achieve different spectral functions in different stack regions
Layer position affects spectral response due to interference phase relationships
expected_advantages: Physical separation of UV and SWIR functions may improve spectral isolation
Complementary to symmetric alternating stacks in other routes
May achieve better dual-band balance through functional segmentation
known_risks: Asymmetric design may create unwanted interference between sections
May not improve performance over symmetric alternating stack
Optimization complexity increases with functional segmentation
